title: Optical spectroscopy of composite fermion edge states in the fractional quantum Hall effect
authors: Maria Sebastian, Ashutosh Singh, Alexey Belyanin
abstract: We show that edge states in fractional quantum Hall effect samples can be selectively probed and excited with sub-terahertz optical spectroscopy. Using the composite fermion (CF) mean-field framework, which maps the strongly correlated fractional quantum Hall problem onto an effective integer quantum Hall problem, we calculate the absorbance spectrum for the Jain sequence of filling fractions including both bulk and edge states. The CF edge-state absorption peaks appear in the millimeter-wave to sub-terahertz range, e.g., 60-500 GHz at B = 10 T in GaAs, i.e. they are blueshifted with respect to the bulk CF cyclotron frequency but are well below the integer quantum Hall cyclotron frequency scale at the same magnetic fields. The number of resolved peaks in each series of the absorption spectrum counts the filled Lambda-levels and fingerprints the fraction. Inversion symmetry breaking near the edge activates optical transitions forbidden in the bulk and enables second-order nonlinear processes in electric-dipole approximation. The absolute frequency scale of the spectrum is set by the CF effective mass, which is generated entirely by electron-electron interactions, so the absorption spectrum provides a direct optical probe of this interaction-induced mass.
summary: This theoretical work demonstrates how sub-terahertz optical spectroscopy can be used to selectively probe the edge states in Fractional Quantum Hall systems. By employing the Composite Fermion mean-field theory, the authors calculate characteristic absorption peaks whose frequency scale directly reveals the electron-electron interaction-induced effective mass. This offers a powerful, non-invasive optical diagnostic tool for understanding strongly correlated quantum matter.
main_problem: The goal is to selectively probe and excite the edge states present in Fractional Quantum Hall (FQH) effect samples using sub-terahertz optical spectroscopy.
main_result: The calculated edge-state absorption peaks appear in the millimeter-wave to sub-terahertz range, providing a direct optical probe of the electron-electron interaction-induced effective mass ($m_{CF}^*$).
method: The authors calculated the absorbance spectrum using the Composite Fermion (CF) mean-field framework, analyzing the difference between $\hat{y}$- and $\hat{x}$-polarized absorption to isolate edge contributions.
model_or_system: The system is a 2D electron gas in the FQH regime, modeled by mapping the strongly correlated problem onto an effective integer quantum Hall problem using Composite Fermions. The analysis involves solving a differential equation derived from the CF Hamiltonian.
key_observables: CF edge-state absorption peaks (60–500 GHz at 10 T), the number of resolved peaks (counting filled $\Lambda$-levels), and the difference spectrum $A^{\hat{y}} - A^{\hat{x}}$.

main_assumptions: The calculations are performed within the CF mean-field approximation, and the edge state contribution is isolated by calculating the difference spectrum $A^{\hat{y}} - A^{\hat{x}}$.

paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem (probing FQH edge states), details the theoretical framework (CF mean-field mapping), outlines the calculation of optical response using polarization differences, and presents the key results showing spectral fingerprints and mass determination.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, measurable optical signature (sub-THz absorption) linked directly to the interaction physics ($m_{CF}^*$) governing strongly correlated electron systems, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and many-body dynamics.
